newsitem.title: CANADA: Sask Pool calls for more rail resources.
newsitem.headline: Sask Pool calls for more rail resources.

text.p: Canada's largest grain handler on Monday called on railway companies to add more resources to moving grain to export position.
"We are calling on the railways to dedicate the crews, locomotives, cars and track necessary to get grain moving through the mountains," SWP president Leroy Larsen said.
Heavy snow, extreme cold and equipment failure caused rail delays that led to a backlog of vessels waiting to load grain on Canada's Pacific coast since early January.
At its height on March 5, one ship had waited 62 days to load.
The Canadian Wheat Board said it faces more than C$20 million in demurrage fines.
Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale met with grain handlers and officials from Canadian National Railway Co and CP Rail System in mid-February to devise a plan to expedite shipments.
Rail car unloads at export ports have since come close but continued to fallen short of allocated target levels, CWB statistics show.
